params.body:
Portal's phone screens catch up with the platform, and Portal serves them as JSON to the native Android app (abovebeyond-ai/portal-android).

**The workbench on the phone.** The watch says whether it is safe (the grants' verdict) and what waits for the owner's touch, or one quiet row when the workbench is safe and nothing waits. `/mobile/workbench`, under the Watch tab, has what knocks ticked first and every other project folded under it, and admits through the same options and admit as `/portal/werkbank`. Each project says what the workbench may do there once admitted and what the touch does given the working set; when a working set leaves a selected project out, the screen says which instead of reloading as if all were admitted.

**The voice in Portal.** `/mobile/voice`, from every mobile screen: the conversation the bridge's own page held (WebRTC to the realtime model with a key the voice bridge mints for one conversation, the bridge carrying out the actions). Portal holds no key and carries none of it. The microphone is allowed on this page alone (`Permissions-Policy: microphone=(self)` there, `microphone=()` everywhere else).

**JSON for the app.** `/app/*` on the owner's own session: `watch`, `work`, `fleet`, `systems`, `project/{slug}`, `workbench` (with its options and admit), `voice`, `me`, and a passkey sign-in (`login/options`, `login`, `logout`). Each screen is computed once, in `MobileScreens`, for both the Blade views and the JSON, so the two say the same thing; a test holds every string of each `/app` answer to the matching `/mobile` page. The routes require `X-Portal-App: 1` and are CSRF-exempt behind it (a browser cannot add that header cross-site without a preflight Portal never allows); no owner session answers `401 {"signin": true}`. Language from `Accept-Language`.

**The app's passkey.** `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` names the app's package and signing certificate (`ANDROID_APPS`, package=SHA-256, comma-separated), and both assertion checks (sign-in, admission) accept the origin Android gives an assertion made in the app, `android:apk-key-hash:<the certificate's SHA-256, base64url>`, beside Portal's own. Tested with a real ES256 assertion in Credential Manager's shape for both.

Also fixed on the way: a silent job is now red on the phone's Systems (the template checked a state Cadence never returns), and the phone's workbench times are in Belgian time.

After deploy, `ANDROID_APPS` in Portal's `.env` names the app's certificate; until then assetlinks.json is an empty list and only the site signs.

Tests: 655 of 656 pass; `BuildStampTest` fails in a worktree checkout without this change as well. PHPStan and Pint pass.
params.title: Phone screens catch up with Portal, and serve the Android app as JSON
